18/18 (12 offline + 6 live). Real stack: docker Postgres with AsyncPostgresSaver, a genuine Supabase ES256 token, real OpenAI; 6 real turns, $0.0322 measured by the feature itself. Proved in production: chat turn usage matches its row; multi-intent stream converges on synthesize with usage on the done event (49,152/52,322 input tokens served from cache); a real provider 403 still recorded latency 6460ms + cost $0.0175 (the 1a494e9 fix under a real failure); the migration applied to real Postgres with its 3 indexes; a dated snapshot model name priced correctly; unauthenticated /agent/* -> 401. Found a defect no offline test could: /agent/chat left every row running and lost the assistant reply - fixed in bffdf44. ROOT-CAUSED afterwards and the first attribution CORRECTED: this is a regression introduced by this branch, NOT a pre-existing bug (main's exact background-task shape persists everything). It is an application-level deadlock: the handler flushes finish() onto the request session, holding an uncommitted row lock on agent_runs; the background task this branch added then UPDATEs the same row on a second connection and blocks; the dependency teardown that would COMMIT only runs after background tasks. pg_stat_activity shows the pair (request: idle in transaction/ClientRead on UPDATE status; background: active/Lock:transactionid on UPDATE background_*). Each failing turn also leaked an idle-in-transaction connection. Committing before returning releases the lock first; verified live with background_llm_calls=1/tokens=1341/ms=1426 and zero lock waits. Real UUIDs also overflowed the dashboard table; ids truncated to 8 with the full value in title. Advisory: the root cause of the missing teardown commit is unproven and may affect other handlers; title on a span is weak for accessibility/copy.

Independent review of bffdf44 (spec pass / quality approved). Commit placement correct on all three _finalize call sites: interrupt commits only the run row, the exception path only the deliberate fallback reply plus the failed row (user message and start() already committed pre-graph; graph tools use their own session_scope). No double-commit with the pre-graph commit, no SQLite lock contention, and add_background now updates an already-committed row instead of racing the teardown. Two gaps raised, both fixed in 7ec5280: a failed commit left the session dirty so the teardown commit would raise (rollback added), and the regression test pinned only the row, not the assistant reply (assertion added). Advisory: why the teardown commit did not reach Postgres is still unproven - other handlers relying solely on it share the exposure.

Controlled live-server experiments isolating why the run row stayed running. get_session instrumented: teardown never executed for a failing turn (CREATE only, no exception). Variables isolated one at a time - custom BaseHTTPMiddleware disabled (still failed), no-op background task (passed), 3s sleep background task (passed, and teardown ran before the sleep finished), _isolated_factory(session) alone (passed), main's exact background-task shape without run_id/session_factory (passed, assistant message persisted). Only passing run_id+session_factory reproduced it. pg_stat_activity confirmed the app-level deadlock on the agent_runs row. Conclusion: get_session is sound and main is unaffected; the defect was introduced by this branch and is fixed by committing before the handler returns. Verified post-fix on the live stack: background columns written, reply persisted, zero lock waits.
